strategy_title: Persistent Kernel Causes Shared Memory Occupancy Collapse
strategy_description: Increasing BLOCK_N from 32 to 128 (and adding a persistent loop) caused dynamic shared memory per block to jump from ~25 KB to ~156 KB, which reduced Block Limit Shared Mem from 9 to 1 block per SM. This collapsed theoretical occupancy from 56% to 6.25%, making the persistent loop useless — each SM can only hold 1 block anyway. The stall profile shifted from shared-memory bank conflicts (MIO stalls, 65% of CPI) to L1TEX stalls (80% of CPI), and duration increased 22x (9.6 µs → 210 µs).
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: small tile, high shared mem bank conflicts but fits multiple blocks/SM
BLOCK_M = 16; BLOCK_N = 32; BLOCK_K = 128
# dynamic_smem ~25 KB/block → Block Limit Shared Mem = 9
# Theoretical occupancy = 56%
grid = (32,)  # 0.03 waves/SM
fast_pseudocode:
# After (regressed): larger tile + persistent loop, but smem blows up
BLOCK_M = 16; BLOCK_N = 128; BLOCK_K = 128
# dynamic_smem ~156 KB/block → Block Limit Shared Mem = 1
# Theoretical occupancy = 6.25% — same as achieved, no headroom
grid = (min(num_tiles, 132),)
for tile_id in range(pid_start, num_tiles, num_programs):  # persistent loop
    ...  # each SM still only runs 1 block, loop adds overhead
applicable_when: Persistent kernel loops help when the grid is smaller than SM count AND increasing tile size does NOT push dynamic shared memory above the per-SM shared memory budget divided by desired blocks-per-SM.
do_not_apply_when: Do NOT increase tile size (BLOCK_N, BLOCK_M) when the resulting dynamic shared memory per block exceeds ~(total_smem_per_SM / target_blocks_per_SM). On H200 with 228 KB shared mem per SM, a 156 KB/block allocation limits to 1 block/SM, making persistent loops pointless and adding instruction overhead. Also avoid when the problem is already latency-bound by a tiny grid — the persistent loop cannot create more parallelism than the tile count allows.
framework_notes: In Triton, BLOCK_N directly controls the shared memory tile size for the B matrix. Doubling BLOCK_N roughly doubles shared memory usage. Check Block Limit Shared Mem in NCU Occupancy section before committing to larger tiles. The autotune configs in this attempt did not vary BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N (they were left as constexprs), so autotune only swept num_warps/num_stages — providing no benefit for the tile-size problem.
